input.rationale: Section 13.5 starts from the right place (Developments created solely by Corio are owned by Corio and Commerce One assigns any claim of ownership), but the carve-out hands ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis. That is an assignment of our own IP to the Vendor and falls in walk-away territory, so the clause fails both the preferred and fallback positions. There is also no licence back for Commerce One materials embedded in Developments, no statement that the parties will not jointly own IP, and no clause preserving our rights in Corio and Customer data or limiting Commerce One's use of that data. We therefore delete the ownership flip, add the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free embedded-IP licence, confirm no joint ownership, and add a short data-ownership sentence, keeping the rest of Section 13 intact. Vendor retention of its own Software (Section 2.8) and of pre-existing materials is unaffected and acceptable.

mappings.quote: Commerce One hereby retains all of its right, title, and interest in and to the Software, including all copyrights, patents, trade secret rights, trademarks and other intellectual property rights therein.

mappings.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.

proposal.summary: Corio owns Developments outright; licence-back for embedded Commerce One IP; no joint ownership; Corio retains all rights in its data
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We delete Commerce One's ability to take ownership of Developments created solely by Corio, add a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Commerce One materials embedded in those Developments, confirm the parties will not jointly own IP, and confirm Corio retains all rights in its and its Customers' data with Commerce One limited to processing it solely to provide the services. This is our preferred IP position.
